name: trust_remote_code=True in HuggingFace transformers executes arbitrary Python code from the model repository
symptom: You call AutoModel.from_pretrained() with trust_remote_code=True on a malicious model repository. The repository's custom modeling code executes arbitrary Python code on your machine with your privileges.
root_cause: HuggingFace transformers allows model repositories to include custom Python code (modeling_*.py, configuration_*.py). When trust_remote_code=True, this code is imported and executed. A malicious repository can include code that exfiltrates data, installs backdoors, or destroys files.
workaround: Never set trust_remote_code=True unless you have audited the model repository's code. Prefer models that use standard architectures (no custom code). If you must use trust_remote_code, inspect the repository's Python files first. Consider running in a sandboxed environment.
notes: This is the HuggingFace equivalent of the pickle problem. The trust_remote_code flag is needed for some custom architectures (e.g., early MoE models), but it is a powerful attack surface. Combined with pickle, a malicious model repository has two independent code execution vectors.
